grades._comment: 737: <150 fpm butter, 150-300 excellent, 300-500 firm/normal, 500-600 heavy (pre-inspection), >600 hard landing inspection per Boeing AMM

engines._comment: Exact CFM56 idle and limit N1 percentages are intentionally omitted until a public Boeing/engine-source reference is checked in.

spoilers._comment: The official SDK supplies authoritative speedbrake annunciators but no continuous handle position. Core spoiler position therefore remains on the standard SimConnect percent path.

controls._comment: PMDG 737 writes use the shared adapter, official SDK routes, and the exact 0..300 dimmer LVars defined by the installed PMDG cockpit behavior. Generic AP, gear/flap key-event, and unrelated LVar write paths are intentionally absent.

meta.notes: PMDG 737-800 family profile using the official NG3 SDK and guarded backend-owned event routes. SDK data and writes remain disabled until the user accepts the PMDG SDK EULA.

sources.name: PMDG 737 MSFS SDK and installed aircraft behavior definitions
sources.notes: The installed PMDG 737 SDK manual, PMDG_NG3_SDK.h, connection sample, and 73X_Cockpit_Behavior.xml define the 916-byte NG3 ClientData contract, direct-position control events, data-broadcast requirement, model variants, and mandatory SDK EULA opt-in. The installed header publishes battery, standby-power, transfer-bus, IRS, window-heat, APU, ground-power, bus-powered, gear-handle, autobrake, parking-brake, pack, bleed, anti-ice, yaw-damper, and stabilizer-trim readbacks. The installed behavior defines direct targets for all nine normal flap-handle detents; Flight Fabric confirms them against the standard FLAPS HANDLE INDEX because ClientData publishes flap needles rather than the handle. It also defines 0..300 LVar positions for 16 continuously dimmable controls: OH_CB_PANEL_LIGHT_CONTROL, OH_PANEL_LIGHT_CONTROL, CA_MAIN_PANEL_LIGHT_CONTROL, FO_MAIN_PANEL_LIGHT_CONTROL, CA_BACKGROUND_BRT_CONTROL, CA_AFDS_FLOOD_LIGHT_CONTROL, PED_FLOOD_LIGHT_CONTROL, PED_PANEL_LIGHT_CONTROL, CA_OUTBD_DU_BRIGHT_CONTROL, CA_INBD_DU_BRIGHT_CONTROL, CA_INBD_DU_RDR_BRIGHT_CONTROL, CA_UPPER_DU_BRIGHT_CONTROL, CA_LOWER_DU_BRIGHT_CONTROL, FO_OUTBD_DU_BRIGHT_CONTROL, FO_INBD_DU_BRIGHT_CONTROL, and FO_INBD_DU_RDR_BRIGHT_CONTROL. The cockpit-lighting preset writes those exact positions in four guarded groups and confirms every LVar as a whole percentage. Discrete dome/spot lights, chart/map mechanisms, EFB buttons, CDU internals, and the explicitly inoperative lower-DU inner knob are excluded. Spring-loaded ground-power and APU-generator controls use reviewed ROTOR_BRAKE direction/release sequences. Stable selectors use matching direct SDK event IDs and exact logical readback. Existing NAV1 controls 729/732/733, NAV2 controls 845/848/849, and position-light control 123 retain their reviewed ROTOR_BRAKE compatibility encodings. The installed PMDG SDK assigns direct course-set events #84132 to the captain window and #84133 to the first-officer window. Flight Fabric maps that contract through the clientdata-manifest adapter and checked-in pmdg-737-ng3-clientdata connector. The public source includes Flight Fabric's independently written SDK interoperability mappings but not PMDG headers, manuals, samples, binaries, or other vendor files.

sources.name: Microsoft Flight Simulator Aircraft Radio Navigation Events
sources.notes: NAV1_RADIO_SET and NAV2_RADIO_SET accept Frequency BCD16 payloads and directly set their respective active NAV frequencies. Flight Fabric sends both events in one guarded PMDG command and independently confirms both active-frequency SimVars.

knownIssues: The 737-800 is the first live-validation target; the 600, 700, and 900 family profiles require in-aircraft testing.
SDK readback requires EnableDataBroadcast=1 and the user to accept the PMDG EULA.
The direct NAV and position-light routes are guarded and remain unverified until simulator confirmation.
The paired NAV 1 + NAV 2 active-frequency command uses documented standard simulator events but remains unverified in a live PMDG 737 cockpit.
The paired captain + first-officer MCP course command uses the installed SDK direct-set events but remains unverified in a live PMDG 737 cockpit.
The 16-dimmer cockpit-lighting percentage preset follows the installed 737-800 behavior definitions but remains unverified end to end in the simulator and requires family-variant confirmation.
Initial-power, flap-handle, speedbrake, gear, brake, pack, bleed, anti-ice, and stabilizer-trim writes remain unverified until end-to-end simulator passes are completed.
MCP mode and selector actions remain untested until IAS/Mach, VS, and button behavior are confirmed in the aircraft.
The official SDK exposes speedbrake annunciators but not a continuous handle position; spoiler state stays on standard SimConnect percent telemetry.
